thesis: Second-quarter net sales reached $1.27 billion, up 5%, and the company raised its full-year sales and EPS outlook while increasing planned buybacks, which suggests the operating trend supports a long candidate. The strongest counter-evidence is that comparable sales were flat and an approximately $100 million tariff-refund benefit inflated the margin and EPS headline; that does not overturn the read because both brands posted higher reported sales and the full-year sales outlook was raised. A former CEO's scheduled late-October sex-trafficking trial creates a near-term litigation and reputational event, while the 2024 indictment creates governance history under the fixed rubric.
invalidation: The company withdraws its raised fiscal 2026 sales outlook, or subsequent results show reported brand sales growth reversing alongside materially weaker comparable sales.
sources: Associated Press on the former CEO's scheduled trial: https://apnews.com/article/abercrombie-fitch-ceo-sex-trafficking-trial-jeffries-5d69db86ff7307f10c66f0b276bac695

thesis: Biohaven signed a worldwide licensing agreement with SK Biopharmaceuticals for the Kv7 platform led by opakalim, with $350 million payable at closing, another $50 million in 2027, up to $150 million in development and regulatory milestones, royalties, and transfer of specified future program costs; this suggests materially lower financing and commercialization burden while retaining upside. The strongest counter-evidence is that opakalim remains investigational, pivotal RISE3 results are pending, and Biohaven has disclosed a securities suit challenging prior opakalim and troriluzole statements; this does not overturn the read because the signed agreement creates non-dilutive capital and transfers program costs without requiring Biohaven to build a commercial organization.
invalidation: The licensing agreement is terminated or fails to close, or its disclosed near-term cash and cost-transfer terms are materially reduced.
sources: Biohaven and SK Biopharmaceuticals licensing agreement: https://ir.biohaven.com/news-releases/news-release-details/biohaven-and-sk-biopharmaceuticals-enter-strategic-global

thesis: Kanzhun reported second-quarter revenue growth of 14.1%, operating-income growth of 32.6%, paid-enterprise-customer growth of 10.8%, and monthly-active-user growth of 10.4%, which suggests recurring platform growth supports a long candidate. The strongest counter-evidence is that the 173.1% GAAP net-income increase was dominated by a fair-value investment gain and operating cash flow fell 10.2%; that does not overturn the read because revenue, customer growth, income from operations, and adjusted operating income all improved independently of the investment gain.
invalidation: Paid enterprise customer growth stalls and the company subsequently reports revenue or operating-income growth materially below its disclosed third-quarter range.

thesis: Semtech reported record second-quarter net sales of $341.9 million, up 33% year over year, with GAAP operating margin improving to 16.3% from negative 6.3%, adjusted EPS rising to $0.71 from $0.41, and free cash flow reaching $61.4 million; this suggests data-center and LoRa demand is translating into operating leverage and supports a long candidate. The strongest counter-evidence is that GAAP net income included a $101.4 million tax benefit and the third-quarter outlook depends on a rapid 1.6T product ramp; that does not overturn the read because adjusted operating income, free cash flow, and record backlog independently corroborate the operating improvement.
invalidation: Record backlog fails to convert into revenue, or the company cuts its disclosed third-quarter net-sales or margin outlook because the 1.6T ramp is delayed.
